# Primary-source reading and implementation decisions

This record separates obtained full text, implemented equations, inspected native interfaces and unavailable material. The paper manifest records exact files, versions, dates, hashes and failed URL attempts. Downloading a paper does not itself establish a faithful implementation; each method guide states its deviations.

| Source | Material reviewed and consequence |
|---|---|
| Burer–Monteiro–Zhang | Rank-two objective/coordinate and rounding discussion, alongside the already validated project implementation. Existing sequential updates, near-zero policy, rounding geometry and original-cut selection remain unchanged. Project defaults are not claimed to reproduce every original heuristic mechanism. |
| Benlic–Hao BLS | Sections 2.1–2.4, Algorithms 1–3, perturbation operators/probabilities, stagnation and Table 1. The trajectory continues from the current attractor even when worse than global best. Descent ignores tabu. Repeated actual labels increase jump magnitude. Fixed scan implementation replaces buckets. Tiny floors, transient-best retention and M2 eligibility details are disclosed in the guide. |
| Palubeckis–Krivickiene | The Max-Cut one-flip tabu, aspiration and multistart context. The project implements a clearly specified best-admissible fixed-tenure variant, not the entire transformed-QUBO MST/RRT procedure. |
| Myklebust | Simulated annealing acceptance, temperature and optimized Max-Cut context. Local implementation is expressly a uniform-proposal/geometric-cooling project baseline; no claim of reproducing optimized paper code. |
| Dunning–Gupta–Silberholz | Portfolio evaluation and independent implementations. MQLib is built separately; actual `-l` output determines available identifiers. BURER2002 is never confused with the project's BM, and BLS is not invented as an available identifier. |
| Generic MILP | Derived all four binary-XOR inequalities and checked their truth table, including negative weights. Native PySCIPOpt API handles real incumbent injection, limits, primal/dual/gap/status. This is distinct from SMS's model. |
| SMS paper / thesis | SIAM PDF HTTP 403; the institutional author thesis returned an Anubis access-denied challenge. Neither full text was obtained or claimed read. Integration is grounded in the full pinned C++ source: main input compaction, CLParser flags, McSolution JSON, BasicOcwSolver and warm-start handling. Native equations/model remain upstream rather than reimplemented from an abstract. |
| BiqBin | Paper Sections 3–5: $x^TLx/4$, SDP relaxation, hypermetric inequalities, bounding/branching and feasible heuristic. Reviewed actual C MPI CLI, integer input, hardcoded RNG and JSON output. Only Max-Cut input is exposed, not the paper's general binary-quadratic reformulation API. |
| MADAM | SDP/ADMM method and bounding discussion: inequality slacks, projection, hypermetric strengthening, numerical upper-bound recovery and MPI coordinator/worker branch-and-bound. Inspected params and text solution output. Actual native implementation is built rather than approximated with a generic SDP placeholder. |
| BiqCrunch | Official 2.0 manual and distinct 2012 author preprint of the 2014 bounding paper: Laplacian quadratic objective, reinforced semidefinite bounds, branch/prune logic and converter. Original converter/source establishes the BC factor and dummy-node convention. The 2017 TOMS full paper was not obtained; the official site's 2012a PDF is a different k-cluster article and was correctly rejected under the TOMS title. |
| Goto et al. 2021 | Full primary PMC HTML Methods, including momentum-first bSB Eqs.(15)–(16), sign-force dSB Eqs.(17)–(18), normalization and inelastic walls. PDF endpoints failed; full HTML remains archived and hashed. CPU initialization/ramp/defaults are explicit educational settings. |
| GSB published formulation | Read arXiv:2508.17655v5 Eqs.(3)–(7) and Appendix A; rendered page 2 to verify new-p/old-x update order and denominator. Published Phys. Rev. Applied 25, 044011 (2026), DOI 10.1103/2qd9-x6v8. Retained earlier v1 separately. Appendix A's spectral normalization is distinguished from project RMS default; nonlinear strength is not automatically tuned to chaos. |
| TESB | Full paper methods plus pinned original `tSB.py`, especially SB initialization and `update_b`. Uses actual CPU warm/checking phases and sampled tabu history. The CPU sampled repulsion is not asserted equal to the full gradient of the paper's Hamiltonian penalty. RNG/import environment effects and zero normalization denominator are explicitly handled. |
| SBQA | Full Methods Eqs.(4)–(8), initialization/schedule/threshold context and parameter-sensitivity discussion; rendered page 3. Both Hamilton equations carry 1/R; inter-replica coupling is periodic along replica columns, with log-tanh schedule and additive $10^{-5}$. The local CPU path reproduces these forces with explicit fixed settings, not the paper's auto-tuning or GPU benchmarks. |
| Glass–Feder | Signed planar minimum T-join derivation, face consistency versus noncontractible cycles, toroidal relaxation/bounds and cycle-repair algorithms. Inspected original expanded-dual, matching, painting and generator-cycle routines. Adaptation avoids dense HAPI and checks original row-major embedding and both wraps. |
| Pardella–Liers / Khoshbakht–Weigel | Planar matching, frustration and periodic-boundary/domain-wall distinctions. Local generic signed face-dual T-join solver is identified as its own implementation; it is not claimed to reproduce the specialized high-performance lattice matching code. |
| Rehfeldt–Koch–Shinano / QuBowl | Full sparse exact-solving paper retained and reviewed as research context: reductions, cutting planes, branch-and-cut and parallelization. Official author availability response reviewed; no executable/source obtained. Marked blocked, without substituting SCIP or SMS. |

Primary PDFs and derivatives are in [`papers/`](../../papers/README.md); upstream revisions and original notices in [`external/`](../../external/sources.json). Reading does not establish a new numerical performance claim. Only the bounded verification evidence establishes actual local behavior.
